statements.text: Primary resources (Field resources) are the resources from which we originally get data through interviewing or questionnaires (survey). This type is distinguished by accuracy, but it needs time and effort and is highly expensive to conduct.

Secondary resources (historical resources): we can get data from authorities and agencies that formally work, such as the central agency for mobilization and statistics, internet and media. This type is a good type of resource because it saves time and money.

context.text: Imagine your class wants to know how many hours students in your school spend on their phones each day. You could hand out a questionnaire and interview students yourself, or you could look up figures already published by an official statistics agency. Which choice is the primary resource and which is the secondary one, and what is the advantage of each in time, cost and accuracy?

statements.text: Method of mass population means collecting the data related to the phenomenon of the statistical society. It is used to include all the society, such as the population. It includes all the values and is unbiased, and the outcomes are very accurate.
Advantage 1: using samples saves time, efforts and money.
Advantage 2: it is the only way to collect data about gigantic societies (like fish).
Advantage 3: it is the only method to study some limited societies, such as the two cases below.
A: Check the patient's blood by getting a sample (checking the whole blood leads to death).
B: Check the production of a factory producing electric lamps to determine the validity of the lamp (know for how long the lamp can be used before getting burned).
A disadvantage of sample methods: outcomes are not accurate if the selected sample doesn't represent all the society well; in such a case the sample is called biased.

context.text: The method of collecting data is determined according to the aim and the size of the statistical society under study.
It mainly depends upon selecting a sample from the statistical society that it represents.

statements.text: Biased selection means selecting the sample in a way to satisfy the objectives of the research; this is called a deliberate sample.
Random selection means selecting a sample such that the chance of getting any value from the society is equal.
1. Simple random sample: the simplest type of sample; it can be got from homogeneous societies where selection is related to the size and number of units in the society.

A. If the size of the society is small: when choosing 5 students of a 40-student class, prepare an identical card for each student with name or number, put them in a box, draw a card randomly and return it again; repeat until the sample needed is obtained.

If the size of the society is big (e.g. selecting a sample of 5 students from 800): number the students from 1 to 800, then use the calculator or Excel to give 10 random digits in the field from 0.000 to 0.999, remove the decimal point so the field runs from zero to 999, and discard the digits that are more than 800.
Five non-repeated digits are enough to give the numbers of the sample of students.

When the society to be examined is heterogeneous or made up of qualitative sets that differ in characteristics, it is divided into homogeneous sets according to the characteristics forming it. Each set is called a layer, and the researcher selects a random sample in which each layer is represented according to its size in the society. Such a sample is called the layer sample.

context.text: For example, when we want to know how the students understood a lesson in mathematics we must analyze the outcomes of the test by considering the outcomes of a group of students studied the same topic without the other students; this is not a random selection.
